verdicts.reason: Germany's AGF integrated streaming data into its ratings with its 2017 restructuring; the UK's BARB hybrid (Dovetail fusion of panel and device data) also came after 2014 (TV Player Report 2015, Dovetail later). Introduction came about 3 years late, so partial. Confidence low: BARB article gives no launch date.

evidence.title: AGF Videoforschung (German Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: In 2017 AGF was renamed and restructured so that streaming data are included in the ratings measurement.

evidence.title: Broadcasters' Audience Research Board (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Describes Dovetail Fusion combining panel and device data, without a 2014 launch; SVOD measured from Nov 2021.

verdicts.reading: Worldwide premium sports broadcast rights would rise 14% to $24.2bn in 2014.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: 2014 value of premium sports media rights vs $24.2bn.
verdicts.reason: 'Premium' sports rights is a Deloitte-defined subset; public estimates (SportBusiness, PwC) cover all sports media rights with different scopes (roughly $35-45bn), not this subset.

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2014
evidence.shows: The $24.2bn covers Deloitte's selection of premium leagues; no public series uses the same scope.

verdicts.reading: Global recorded-music performance rights revenue would exceed $1bn for the first time in 2014.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric (floor): IFPI global performance rights revenue 2014 vs $1bn.
verdicts.reason: The measure is IFPI's annual performance-rights line; the 2015 Digital Music Report and secondary analyses could not be retrieved (404 on three URLs), and Wikipedia gives no figure. Not verified, so not graded.

evidence.title: IFPI Digital Music Report 2015
evidence.shows: Fetch returned 404; the IFPI 2014 performance-rights figure could not be retrieved.

evidence.title: Music industry (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Gives 2014 global recorded music market about $14.97bn but no performance-rights figure.

verdicts.reading: VOD users in Sub-Saharan Africa would grow by about one million in 2014.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: 2014 net growth in SSA VOD users vs 1m.
verdicts.reason: No public series counts VOD users in Sub-Saharan Africa for 2013-2014; services (iROKOtv, ShowMax launched 2015) did not publish comparable user counts.

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2014
evidence.shows: Claim names regional VOD user growth; looked for SSA VOD user counts and found none.

verdicts.reading: In 2014 mobile instant messaging would carry about 50 billion messages a day, more than twice SMS (21 billion).
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: global daily MIM messages in 2014 vs 50bn.
verdicts.reason: No public aggregate of MIM traffic exists; only per-app disclosures with different counting (sent vs sent+received): WhatsApp over 30bn a day by January 2015, others (WeChat, Messenger, LINE, iMessage) not disclosed for 2014. Summing partial disclosures would be a proxy.

evidence.title: WhatsApp (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: By early January 2015 WhatsApp had over 30 billion messages every day; no aggregate across apps.

verdicts.reading: In 2014 phablets (smartphones with 5.0-6.9 inch screens) would be a quarter of smartphone sales, about 300 million units.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: 2014 shipments of 5.0-6.9 inch smartphones vs 300m.
verdicts.reason: Public phablet figures use other size bands (IDC: 5.5-7 inch), and trackers with a 5-inch cut-off report shares that imply far larger totals; estimates for the 5.0-6.9 band are not public and published phablet figures span more than a factor of 2 depending on cut-off (D23).

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2014
evidence.shows: Deloitte defines phablets as 5.0-6.9 inch; public trackers use different bands.

verdicts.reading: In 2014 over-55s would show the fastest year-on-year rise in smartphone penetration of any age group across developed markets.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Age-group smartphone penetration change 2013-2014 across developed markets.
verdicts.reason: National surveys (Ofcom, Pew) measure this in single countries with different age bands; no cross-developed-market series. Ofcom pages returned 403. Looked for Ofcom Technology Tracker and Pew 2013-2014 data.

evidence.title: Ofcom Communications Market Report
evidence.shows: Fetch returned 403; UK-only data in any case, not a developed-markets measure.

verdicts.reading: In 2014 the entry price of a ruggedised connected data device for field workers would fall to $250.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Event test: availability of a ruggedised connected device at about $250 in 2014.
verdicts.reason: 'Ruggedised' has no standard (IP rating, MIL-STD) in the claim, and no price census exists; consumer rugged phones and enterprise rugged handhelds differ by an order of magnitude. Looked for 2014 rugged device price data.

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2014
evidence.shows: Claim's device class is undefined; no public price series for rugged enterprise devices.

verdicts.reading: In 2015 one billion wireless IoT devices would ship, up 60%, for an installed base of 2.8 billion.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: 2015 wireless IoT device shipments vs 1bn.
verdicts.reason: IoT counts depend entirely on definition; public 2015 estimates of IoT devices (Gartner 4.9bn 'connected things in use', IHS, Ericsson, Cisco) differ by more than a factor of 2 and none uses Deloitte's 'wireless IoT shipments' scope (D23 range rule).

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2015
evidence.shows: Deloitte's IoT scope excludes phones/PCs and counts wireless shipments; public estimates use other scopes and diverge widely.

verdicts.reading: In 2015 the active base of non-military drones costing $200 or more would exceed one million units for the first time.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric (floor): active base of $200+ civil drones end-2015 vs 1m.
verdicts.reason: No public installed-base series for civil drones by price exists for 2015; DJI (market leader) did not disclose units, FAA registration began only in Dec 2015 and covers the US and all drones over 250 g. Wikipedia UAV and DJI pages give no unit data; FAA release returned 403.

evidence.title: DJI (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: DJI was the largest consumer drone company by 2015; no unit sales or installed base given.

verdicts.reading: About 220,000 3D printers worth $1.6bn would be sold worldwide in 2015.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: 2015 global 3D printer unit sales vs 220,000.
verdicts.reason: Unit counts come from Gartner and Wohlers, whose 2015 figures differ by scope (Wohlers counts desktop units under $5,000 separately); neither source could be retrieved (Gartner and Business Wire 403; Wikipedia gives no figure). Not graded from memory.

evidence.title: 3D printing (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: No 2015 printer unit counts; refers to Gartner/Wohlers reports for market volume.

evidence.title: Gartner 3D printer shipments press release
evidence.shows: Fetch returned 403; 2015 shipment figure not retrievable.

verdicts.reading: Click-and-collect locations in Europe would reach 500,000 in 2015, up 20% on 2014.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: count of European click-and-collect points in 2015.
verdicts.reason: No public census of click-and-collect locations (stores, lockers, parcel shops) in Europe exists; national parcel-network counts use different definitions. Looked for Europe-wide pickup-point counts.

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2015
evidence.shows: The 500,000 figure is Deloitte's own count; no public series of European pickup locations.

verdicts.reading: In 2015 smartphone Li-ion battery technology would improve only modestly, without a breakthrough.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Event/qualitative: no step change in Li-ion energy density in 2015 (annual gain in single digits).
verdicts.reason: Li-ion energy density improved on average 7.5% a year in 2011-2017; 2015 brought lab demonstrations of fast charging but no commercial breakthrough in smartphone batteries.

evidence.title: Lithium-ion battery (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: From 2011 to 2017 progress averaged 7.5% annually; 2015 advances were laboratory fast-charging demonstrations.

verdicts.reading: By end-2015 more than 500 nanosatellites would be in orbit.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric (floor): nanosatellites in orbit at end-2015 vs 500.
verdicts.reason: The measure (Kulu's Nanosatellite & CubeSat Database) reports current cumulative launches (3,417 to July 2026), not an end-2015 in-orbit count, and in-orbit counts depend on decay and launch failures (Antares 2014, Falcon 9 2015). 'In orbit' could also be read as 'launched to date'. No dated figure retrieved.

evidence.title: Nanosats Database
evidence.shows: 3,417 nanosatellites launched as of July 2026; no end-2015 in-orbit count on the landing page.

evidence.title: CubeSat (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: About 75 CubeSats in orbit by 2012; no 2015 figure in text.

verdicts.reading: In 2015 the impetus for IT adoption would swing back from consumers to enterprises.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Qualitative: enterprise-led vs consumer-led technology adoption in 2015.
verdicts.reason: No metric is stated or exists for which segment 'leads' IT adoption; the claim is a narrative judgement.

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2015
evidence.shows: Claim has no measurable indicator.

verdicts.reading: In 2015 short-form online video (under 20 minutes) would be under 3% of all video viewing time on all screens.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D18 rate: short-form share of total video time, 2015.
verdicts.reason: No audience measurement series splits all-screen video time by clip length globally; Nielsen and BARB report TV and online video totals, not short-form share. Looked for a global or national short-form share for 2015.

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2015
evidence.shows: Claim's share is a Deloitte estimate; no public series measures it.

verdicts.reading: US and Canadian millennials would spend over $62bn on media content in 2015.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric (floor): 2015 millennial media-content spend in US and Canada.
verdicts.reason: No public series reports media spending by generation for the US and Canada; BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey uses age bands and different categories, so any figure would be a proxy.

evidence.title: Deloitte TMT Predictions 2015
evidence.shows: The $62bn is a Deloitte model; no public generation-level media spend series.

verdicts.reading: In 2015 print would account for more than 80% of book sales by value worldwide (e-books under 20%).
verdicts.mainstream_test: D18 rate (floor): print share of global book revenue 2015 vs 80%.
verdicts.reason: E-book shares in 2014-2015 were about 4% in Germany, around 20% of US trade (a minority of all US book revenue) and 29-33% in the UK consumer market; with education, professional and Asian markets mostly print, the worldwide e-book share by value was well under 20%. Confidence medium: no single global series was retrieved.

evidence.title: E-book (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: UK e-book share 20% to 33% 2012-2014, 29% in Q1 2015 (Nielsen); Germany 4.3% in 2015 (Wischenbart); US ebooks 12.4% of trade revenue by 2018 (AAP).

verdicts.reading: In 2015 one billion smartphones would be bought as upgrades (replacing a smartphone), generating over $300bn.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: 2015 smartphone upgrade purchases vs 1bn.
verdicts.reason: Trackers report total smartphone shipments (about 1.43bn in 2015), not the split between upgrades and first-time buyers; splits come from surveys or models, not measures.

evidence.title: Smartphone (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Smartphone data are total shipments; no upgrade/first-time split.

verdicts.reading: Global broadband homes would grow about 2% to 715 million by end-2015 (with typical speeds up 15-25%).
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric: global fixed-broadband homes end-2015 vs 715m (hit within 10%).
verdicts.reason: ITU: 10.8 fixed-broadband subscriptions per 100 inhabitants in 2015, about 790-800 million subscriptions on a 7.3-7.4bn population. Subscriptions include business lines, so homes are fewer; 715m is about 10% below total subscriptions and closer to the residential count. Hit, near the edge. The speed sub-claim is not graded.

evidence.title: ITU ICT Facts and Figures 2015
evidence.shows: Global fixed-broadband penetration 10.8 per 100 inhabitants in 2015; world population 7.4bn (about 795m subscriptions).

verdicts.reading: By end-2015, 5% of the 600-650 million NFC-equipped phones would be used at least monthly for in-store contactless payments.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D18 rate: monthly NFC payment users as share of NFC phone base, end-2015.
verdicts.reason: Apple Pay, Android Pay and Samsung Pay did not publish active-user counts for 2015, and no tracker measures monthly in-store use across the NFC phone base. Survey proxies (US share of iPhone 6 owners using Apple Pay) cover other populations.

evidence.title: Near-field communication (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: No NFC payment usage counts for 2015.

verdicts.reading: By end-2016 fewer than 25% of IT jobs in developed countries would be held by women.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D18 rate (ceiling): women's share of IT jobs in developed countries 2016 vs 25%.
verdicts.reason: US 2016: women 25.5% of computer and mathematical occupations (CPS), lower in core IT roles (software developers 20.0%, network admins 17.1%); EU 2015: 16.0% of ICT specialists. The combined developed-country share is about 20%, under 25%.

evidence.title: BLS CPS 2016 annual averages, Table 11: Employed persons by detailed occupation, sex, race
evidence.shows: Women 25.5% of computer and mathematical occupations; 20.0% of software developers; 17.1% of network and computer systems administrators.

evidence.title: Eurostat: ICT specialists in employment
evidence.shows: Women were 16.0% of EU ICT specialists in 2015.
